explicit_evidence_changes.baseline: A Hellobike robotaxi struck two pedestrians in Zhuzhou, trapping one person under the vehicle; both were taken to hospital and the operator suspended local service.
explicit_evidence_changes.candidate: On 6 December 2025, a Hellobike robotaxi collision in Zhuzhou injured two people. Reporting described bystanders and police lifting the vehicle to free a trapped person; hospital staff confirmed both injured people were taken for treatment. Hellobike suspended local autonomous-driving operations, and booking attempts returned out of service. The city’s service line confirmed the suspension on 15 December with no known resumption date. On 29 December traffic police said they had gathered evidence at Hellobike’s headquarters and commissioned a professional technical and safety inspection. No final fault determination, inspection result or exact driving/control state was established in the reviewed sources.

baseline.factual_basis: Jiemian reported that a Level 4 test vehicle struck two pedestrians on a wet road, one of whom became trapped. Both were hospitalised. Police had not announced a fault determination, and the operator suspended service. The available report did not conclusively identify the autonomous-driving stack or operating mode at the moment of collision.
baseline.governance_interpretation: The collision and hospital treatment are reported, and local service was suspended. The operational restriction is supported. The AI safety outcome remains unresolved because driving mode and control telemetry are unavailable; suspension does not establish fault.
baseline.significance_to_cam: The case demonstrates the need to preserve safety consequences while withholding mechanism attribution until vehicle state, operational design domain and control evidence are available.
assessment_boundaries: Police had not published a fault determination in the reviewed evidence.
The precise ADS stack, safety-operator status and injury prognosis remain uncertain.

candidate.factual_basis: Jiemian describes December 6 footage of a vehicle at a crosswalk and people lifting it to release a trapped person. Its accounts of slick roads are resident reports, not a determined crash cause. Nandu’s follow-up attributes confirmation of both injured people’s hospital admission to hospital staff. Customer-service suspension, unavailable bookings and vehicle-removal videos are different response evidence. The municipal service line confirmed suspended operations on December 15. Traffic police told Nandu on December 29 that they had visited the platform headquarters to obtain evidence and requested professional technical and safety inspection; possible rectification was conditional on problems being found. No reviewed result establishes fault, a particular ADS stack, autonomous versus remote control at collision, the safety-operator state or permanent injury. Jiemian’s separate November 28 passenger account and disputed remote takeover are not merged into this event.
candidate.governance_interpretation: Physical consequences and suspension are supported by attributed reporting. Later municipal confirmation strengthens the service-restriction evidence. Investigative steps establish an inquiry, not its result. The exact protective control and its activation or effectiveness remain unknown, so the occurrence does not establish either control failure polarity.
candidate.significance_to_cam: The case demonstrates the need to preserve safety consequences while withholding mechanism attribution until vehicle state, operational design domain and control evidence are available.
assessment_boundaries: Road conditions are reported context, not a determined cause.
The active ADS, vehicle model, driving mode and safety-operator state are unknown; general fleet capabilities do not resolve this trip.
Police evidence collection and a commissioned inspection are not a final finding or verified remedial implementation.
Hospital treatment is reported; detailed diagnoses and prognosis are unavailable.
November 28 is a separate occurrence and its disputed takeover account does not establish December 6 control conditions.
